description: The first READ fails, with no successful read standing in front of it. CUSTFILE is seeded with row 1 of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt - a real 500-byte record, deliberately present - and the very first READ at app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L93 reports '30', the permanent I/O error. The record is therefore never read and never displayed: L94's test for '00' fails, so the display sitting inside that arm at L96 does not run, and because Z-ABEND-PROGRAM ends the enclave the mainline's own display at L78 is never reached either. That absence is the whole assertion. A dataset holding a record is not the same input as a dataset holding none, and an implementation that emitted the row it had been handed - prefetched, buffered, or displayed before the status was tested - would be caught here and nowhere else in this folder, because every other read failure has at least one record image standing ahead of it to hide behind. It brackets case15 from the other side: case15 fails the third READ after two records have already been displayed, and this one fails at the first read ordinal, where there is no partial output at all to mask an ordering mistake. Trace: L71 emits the opening banner. 0000-CUSTFILE-OPEN opens INPUT and sees '00' at L121, moves 0, satisfies 88 APPL-AOK at L126 and CONTINUEs without emitting a line - the transient 8 from L119 is overwritten before anything can observe it, so the open paragraph's own error line at L129 is not reachable. The PERFORM UNTIL at L74 tests its condition first and END-OF-FILE is still 'N' from its VALUE clause at L65, so the body runs. 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT reads and gets '30': L94's '00' test fails and L98's '10' test fails too, so L101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT; 88 APPL-AOK at L104 is then false and 88 APPL-EOF - VALUE 16 - at L107 is false as well, and both being false at once on the very first loop iteration is the earliest point in the program at which that combination is observable (gate G50). Control therefore reaches the fatal arm at L110-L113: the error literal, MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS, Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and Z-ABEND-PROGRAM, whose CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158 ends the enclave. Nothing follows it - PERFORM 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE at L83 never runs, so no close-failure line is reachable, and the L85 banner is never emitted. The contrast with case04 is the substance of why both cases exist, because one IF ladder - L94, L98, L104, L107 - routes the two runs to opposite arms from the same starting point of 'the first READ produced no record'. case04 seeds an empty dataset: its first READ reports '10', APPL-RESULT becomes 16 at L99, 88 APPL-EOF holds at L107, L108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE, the loop ends quietly, the CLOSE succeeds silently, the L85 banner is emitted and the return code is 0. This case seeds a record: its first READ reports '30', APPL-RESULT becomes 12 at L101, 88 APPL-EOF is false, the fatal arm runs, the CLOSE is never performed, no closing banner appears and the return code is 12. An implementation that collapsed 'no record available' into a single outcome would pass one of the pair and fail the other, which is exactly what the pair is for. The error text is the long-form 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' at L110, where the open paragraph at L129 names the DD instead and the close paragraph at L147 is long-form again; the three wordings disagree in the source, and practice B5 keeps them disagreeing rather than normalising them to one phrasing. The status line is 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0030', and both halves of it are genuine output rather than an unfinished expectation. The NNNN inside the literal at L168 and L172 is placeholder text the program never substitutes - it is emitted verbatim, with the operand appended after it - and the operand is exactly four characters because IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at L57-L59, read mechanically from the declaration rather than from prose (practice B11). '30' is all numeric and IO-STAT1 is '3' rather than '9', so L162's condition is false and the ELSE arm at L169-L173 renders it: MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which places '3' at position 3 and '0' at position 4 and gives '0030' - not '003', and not '0300'. The return code is 12, from MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT at L101, the same statement case15 takes its 12 from and a different one from the L124 the open-failure cases use; 16 is loop-control state belonging to case04's APPL-EOF path and never leaves this program as an exit code, since CBCUS01C references RETURN-CODE nowhere at all. The unit is the tasklet of customer.CustomerFileReaderJob - unitKind BATCH_JOB - so the four retained lines and the non-zero exit are observed together at step level with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51), and the name is a job by name only: the COBOL reads and prints, computes nothing and writes no dataset record, which is why expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion rather than an omission (rule R1). Because no record is ever displayed, this case asserts no 500-byte width and no FILLER span even though its input carries one - cases 01 and 11 own gates G19 and G21. Rows are read as US-ASCII, stated explicitly and never left to the platform default (practice B8). Statically derived: every expected value here comes from the COBOL source, the CVCUS01Y byte layout, the app/jcl/READCUST.jcl STEP05 contract - a bare EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C with no PARM, hence no job parameter - and the real app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt row, and none of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution, which the eight blockers in AAP 0.7.6 make impossible in this environment; the deviation is recorded there as risk R-A (practice B12).
